desc: Ideation: discovered that "flip at most once" is FALSE — parking expensive A=B=1 bits (flip off early, on late) can help; derived sequence structure (offs decreasing C, then ons increasing C, with parked set P ⊆ {A=B=1}); derived cost formula and marginal Δ formula for adding a parked bit; sketched exchange proof that optimal P = top-K by C among A=B=1 bits.

Rigorously verify the threshold-property exchange argument and the ordering claims (offs before ons; offs decreasing C; ons increasing C; A=B=0 bits never flipped; S0/S1 bits flipped exactly once; A=B=1 bits flipped 0 or 2 times) — validated via 7000 random/targeted tests where fast solver (which hard-codes these) matches exact Dijkstra over 2^N hypercube.
Implement brute-force solver (Dijkstra over 2^N states, N ≤ 12) for validation.

Implement candidate solver: W0, S0, S1, D sorted desc; cost(0) via prefix walk; iterate K=1..|D| updating cost via Δ formula using 4 Fenwick trees (count/sum over compressed C) for O and U; answer = min_K cost(K); O(N log N).

Cross-validate candidate vs brute force on 4000 random + 3000 targeted small cases, plus best-over-all-subsets check confirming threshold property; edge cases (A=B→0, single bits, cost-0 flip, Sample 1=16, Sample 2=0, parking-helpful=105, parking-harmful=383) all pass.

Write final production solve(): read N, A, B, C from stdin; run validated solve_fast logic; print answer; strip test harness; ensure O(N log N) and Python int arithmetic; handle edge cases (no flips → 0, empty D, all C equal).
